THE REAL PROXY: HOW CHINA PROJECTS ITS AGGRESSION WHILE UNDERMINING PHILIPPINE SOVEREIGNTY | China’s repeated accusations that the Philippines is acting as a “pawn” of the United States are not only false—they are strategically designed to deflect attention from its own unlawful and provocative actions in the West Philippine Sea.

This is textbook narrative inversion: flip the aggressor into the victim, and cast the rightful defender as a foreign proxy. But facts remain stubborn.

The Philippines does not need foreign permission to uphold its sovereignty. Our position is anchored in international law, specifically the 2016 Arbitral Award—an independent legal victory that China has never accepted and now seeks to erase through coercion and disinformation.

It is not Philippines that has built artificial islands. It is not Filipino ships that fire water cannons, execute dangerous maneuvers, or block lawful resupply missions. These are Beijing’s actions, not ours.

When China labels the Philippines a “pawn,” it is a projection—because it is their narrative that is doing the bidding of a larger ambition: eroding the rule of law to justify expansionism.

Sovereignty is not aggression. Compliance with international law is not provocation. And unity with democratic partners is not subservience—it is strategy, born of necessity.
